stem: A class of Grade 10 learners recorded {=what}. The data set is $\{{=x0}\text{ {=unit}}, {=x1}\text{ {=unit}}, {=x2}\text{ {=unit}}, {=x3}\text{ {=unit}}, {=x4}\text{ {=unit}}, {=x5}\text{ {=unit}}\}$. Which of the following correctly categorises the data set and gives the reason?

choices.correct: Quantitative continuous, because the values are measurements, written as real numbers

distractors.text: Quantitative discrete, because the data set is a short list of separate values
Qualitative categorical, because the values only sort the learners into groups
Qualitative anecdotal, because the values only describe the learners

solution: The values are numbers, so the data set of {=what} is quantitative, not qualitative.
Each value is a measurement in {=unit}, written as a decimal number, so the data set cannot be represented by integers.
A measurement written as real numbers is continuous. Therefore the data set is quantitative continuous.
notes:
Standard tier: the book's measurement exercise (ex10-7-1) with a reason added to the options. Values are drawn as scaled integers and shown with fixed(..., dp) so every value keeps its decimals (e.g. 1.70 m); the pool excludes any value that would print as a whole number, so no value looks like a count (the whole-number twist is the advanced family wholenumbers-measure). Units are shown in text inside the math. Direction is fixed (always continuous) so the swap distractor carries the single id measurement-called-discrete.

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit): context-null: the spec set "context" (a fixed word problem's situation, in words) to "A class of Grade 10 learners each record one measurement. The class is fixed; only the thing measured, its unit and the six values change." and its own text says what varies. The stem varies the wording itself, through {=what} and {=unit}, drawn from six measurements, each with its own unit, range and decimals, so it is not a fixed-context word problem. A family with a fixed context may vary only numbers (families/spec.py _stem_holes_are_numbers; extraction-pipeline §3.9), so every attempt was refused ('the stem hole {=...} produced a word') and the family produced no item. A family whose wording is drawn from a curated table is written with "context": null, as this objective's siblings anecdotal-set, categorical-set, counting-categorical and paired-questions are, and its stems are still judged one by one by the blind grader. The former context text is kept above; the stem, params, answer, options and worked solution are unchanged.
